newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Dec 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and her Indian counterpart Deve Gowda are likely to hold a two-day summit in New Delhi on December 10 and 11, which is expected to be capped by the signing of a water sharing agreement.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina yesterday expressed her government's firm commitment for separation of judiciary from the executive to ensure justice.

Bangladesh will strive to reach a permanent agreement with India for sharing the Ganges water during the next round official level talks which will be followed by a visit of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to New Delhi.

Water Resources Minister Abdur Razzak yesterday said 75 projects at a cost of Taka 199.05 crore had been completed till June 1995 and another 93 projects had been taken during current financial year for developing of rivers and protection of their banks.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Tuesday her government was sincerely trying to uproot terrorism from the society and directed police to play a leading role in that effort.
The World Bank has suggested Bangladesh government to accelerate public sector reforms to attain its goal of a 7 percent growth in the national economy to alleviate poverty from grassroot.
India has granted a wide range of tariff concessions covering over 200 items produced in and are exportable from Bangladesh.
Agriculture Minister Matia Chowdhury Tuesday made a blistering attack on donors for overloking the "willful corruption and mismanagement" in fertilizer distribution during the past regime.
